page0.text:
"..."
"..."
Her gaze is painfully unrelenting.
While my knife rhythmically chops tofu, Saber is sitting in a dignified seiza posture,
staring intently at my face.

page1.text:
"I'm going to go to school like I usually do."
We haven't seen eye to eye since I suggested doing so.
Saber is against it, of course.
She says it's too dangerous to let her Master go out alone.
But I have my own life to worry about.

page2.text:
Fuji-nee will get suspicious if I miss class, and I'll never know what's happening outside if I stay cooped up at home.
Besides, we might tip off the other Masters if Saber goes outside.
I think it's worth going out on my own to scout out the terrain.

page3.text:
"Masters aren't supposed to fight in public view, right? So it should be safe during the day. As long as I stay in places with a lot of people, they won't attack me."
Saber disagreed, saying that it wasn't a guarantee of safety.
...To be honest, I lost my temper at how overprotective she was being, and stubbornly insisted on going to school, so that's where we are now.

page4.text:
"..."
Saber's gaze is painful because she's angry at me.

page5.text:
Lesson of the day:
She knows how to hold a grudge. And she's pretty emotional about it too, so she can be a handful.
I'd better be careful not to get into any shouting matches with her in the future.

page6.text:
"...So hard-headed."
"What did you just say, Shirou?"
"Oh, I was just talking to myself. I said, this tofu's really hard."
...
And her hearing's too damn sharp! Definitely not the sort of person you'd want to have a cold war with.

page7.text:
"Hm? Oh, it's that time arleady."
The doorbell rings, and I hear the front door open.
Sakura announces herself a second later.

page8.text: "Oh, I lost thirty minutes arguing with Saber."

page9.text:
Still, I'm mostly finished making breakfast.
I thought about making sandwiches to make Saber happy, but she didn't look like she was in the mood, so I won't.
Japanese people eat rice.
I resist the violence of her gaze by making her follow the old adage, 'when in Rome.'

page10.text:
"Good morning, Senpai. Are you already finished making breakfast?"
"Yeah, I just finished cleaning up. Morning, Sakura. Fuji-nee should be here soon, so help me set the table."

page11.text:
"Okay. I'll help."
Sakura sets her bag down in the living room and greets Saber.

page12.text:
"Good morning, Saber. Did you sleep well last night?"
"Yes. The room is quite new to me, but I've gotten accustomed to the house."
...Oh, they're talking.
They didn't yesterday, but Sakura seems to have accepted her.

page13.text:
"Thank you for waiting, Senpai. How do you want me to set the table?"
"Mm, one big plate and four small plates for the four of us. The salad's ready, so go ahead and dress it however you want."
"All right. Wow, are we having German potato salad today?
You're really going all-out with the Western breakfast."

page14.text:
As she expresses her surprise, Sakura scoops the large serving of potato salad onto the big plate and garnishes it.
I'd like to object that the only Western thing about this meal is the salad, though.
...I'd like to further point out that this isn't a concession to Saber. I just felt like making potato salad.

page15.text:
"Oh, that smells nice. May I have a taste?"
"Sure, but it's hot. And maybe a little sweet."
"Hm?"
Sakura uses a pair of long frying chopsticks to sample the potatoes I'm cooking.

page16.text:
"Mmm... Oh, that really is sweet. That doesn't come from the onions, does it?"
She licks her lips as she considers the recipe.

page17.text:
...
Watching her, I'm...surprised.
I've seen Sakura taste test food plenty of times, but from this close, was she always so charming?

page18.text:
"Yeah, it's good, Senpai! I like how you seasoned it!"
She must be fond of it, because she enthusiastically scoops potatoes into the big plate.
That's the usual Sakura.
I'm relieved to feel my surprise draining away.

page19.text:
"Sakura."
"Yes? What is it?"
She's the same old Sakura.
She's no different than she was yesterday.

page20.text:
"Shinji—"
I stop just short of asking her what happened after he went home last night.
If Shinji has a grudge against me for yesterday, then I doubt he would've let Sakura come over.

page21.text:
Shinji may be a Master belonging to a family of mages, but that has nothing to do with Sakura.
She won't be pulled into this war.

page22.text:
Still, I worry for her.
If something happens that causes Shinji to dump on Sakura all the Matou family affairs, the Holy Grail War, and the fight between Masters, then she'll definitely be involved.
I have to prevent that, no matter what.

page24.text:
"Okay.
...By the way, please don't talk to my brother today.
He was acting off last night. I think he's in a bad mood, so he might say something weird to you."

page25.text:
...
I need to make sure Sakura doesn't know what happened.

page26.text:
...I know why Shinji's acting that way, of course.
He went off the rails last night.
He lost his status as a Master, and his grandfather berated him.
Considering Shinji's personality, he must be seriously pissed at me.

page27.text:
"Kuh..."
Sakura doesn't know anything.
She's ignorant of her brother's situation and her family's secrets.
Then...is it safe for her to keep living with Shinji?
Shinji hasn't given up.
I can't rule out the chance that he might do something awful to his sister.

page28.text:
"...Um, Senpai? I'm sorry for causing you trouble so early in the morning."
"Silly, don't say that. You aren't any trouble."

page29.text:
...I'm the one causing trouble for you.
I should have forseen this situation after fighting Shinji.
I need to think... To come up with a way that Sakura can keep living her life.
To find a way to let her keep smiling like she always has.

page30.text:
Breakfast ends in a gloomy mood.
I don't know why, but Fuji-nee never showed up, and Sakura ate in silence the whole time.
Saber's always been stoic, and I'm not exactly talkative, either.
We clean up quickly after breakfast, and Sakura leaves forty minutes early for morning practice.

page31.text:
"...Um, I'll be going now, Senpai."
Sakura forces a smile and puts on her shoes.

page32.text: "Yeah. Don't be too hard on yourself at club. I know you've been pushing yourself because you haven't been feeling well. Just go through the motions and have tea in the back. If Mitsuzuri has a problem with it, just tell her it's a favor to me."

page33.text:
"Okay. The captain will be happy to hear that."
The front door slides open with a clatter.
Sakura bows, turns to leave,
and runs smack into the door.

page35.text:
"H-hey, are you okay!? Is your nose bleeding!?"
"Y-yeah, I'm ogay. I'd die of embarrassbent if you saw me get a nosebleed."
Sakura stands up unsteadily.
Surely, that accident happened because she wasn't paying attention...right?

page36.text:
"Are you sure you're feeling all right? You looked more like you fainted, rather than just running into the door.  If you're feeling dizzy today, then—"
"Huh? That's not what happened. I just wasn't paying attention. I'm so embarrassed."
"..."

page37.text:
"I'll be going on ahead, Senpai. I'll let Ms. Fujimura know that breakfast was delicious today."
Sakura leaves without further incident, trying to downplay my worries.

page38.text:
...
She does look full of energy.
If she's tired, maybe it's mental rather than physical fatigue.

page39.text:
"...There's still Shinji to deal with. I can't let things stay like this..."
I say that, but I don't have any clear solutions.
I can't consult Saber about this, nor can I tell Sakura the truth. Fuji-nee's completely out, of course.
